newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Moslems leave Serb parliament over voting rights.
newsitem.headline: Moslems leave Serb parliament over voting rights.

text.p: Moslem and Croat members walked out of the Bosnian Serb parliament on Wednesday when their Serb colleagues elected to deny them voting rights, the Yugoslav state news agency Tanjug reported.

The Serb deputies ruled that because the Moslem and Croat parliamentarians had refused to take an oath of allegiance to the Bosnian Serb Republic they had no right to participate in the assembly's decision-making, Tanjug said.
At last month's inaugural parliamentary session the Moslem and Croat deputies objected to elements of the oath which related to the Serbs' traditional Orthodox Christian faith.
The Bosnian Serb news agency SRNA confirmed Wednesday's ruling, but made no mention of the walk-out.
Deputies of the Moslem-based parties said they were "legitimate and legally elected and therefore have the full right to vote", the agency reported.
According to SRNA's report, deputy speaker Nikola Poplasen said the Moslems and Croats relinquished the right to vote when they refused to take the oath as required by a procedural rule.
Poplasen said it was necessary to work under that rule until a new one was adopted.

Another news agency, Fonet, quoted the parliamentary leader of the Moslem-based Party of Democratic Action (SDA), Safed Bico, as saying the legitimacy of his deputies had been brought into question and they had decided to withdraw until "conditions for legal work on an equal basis were created".

International mediators have struggled to create unified multi-ethnic democratic institutions since September's Bosnian national elections. They warn that Bosnia is in danger of slipping back to war if the unified bodies cannot work together.
